subject: Frontloaded procurement and cloud brokerage sync: NovaApps dedicated pool
messages:
From: Tim Clarke <tim.clarke@novaapps.com>
To: rachel_kim@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@novaapps.com
Date: 2025-10-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated pool sizing + ability to frontload procurement

Rachel —

Thanks for taking this early. We just finished an internal sizing exercise and want to explore frontloading hardware procurement tied to our Q1 commit. Key asks:

- Can Redwood coordinate partial OEM orders to reduce our go-live risk (we're on a hard deadline mid-Q2)?
- If we place a tranche order, what are realistic OEM lead times and how do you typically broker cloud burst capacity while waiting for physical shipment?
- Any playbook for mixing a smaller dedicated pool + cloud-brokered burst credits so we can ramp without immediate full-reserve purchase?

I'm attaching our RFP (high level). Would like a short call this week to align on timelines and mutual action items.

Attachments: NovaApps_RFP_v2.pdf (summary + required throughput)

Best,
Tim Clarke
Head of Infra, NovaApps
Tim Clarke
From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>

Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2025-10-30T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool sizing + ability to frontload procurement

Tim —

Appreciate the RFP and the timeline clarity. High level: yes, we can combine a frontloaded OEM tranche + staged reserved capacity with a cloud brokerage backstop. A few quick clarifying points so we come to the call prepared:

1) Target go‑live: you mentioned mid‑Q2 — is the hard date 2026‑04‑15 or a rolling window?
2) Peak baseline: the RFP lists 120 p95 rps for generation. What sustained token throughput do you expect (tokens/min) during ramp weeks 1–6?
3) Model tolerance: are you comfortable starting on a faster-ship SKU that requires 8‑bit quantization steps we can validate?

I'll loop in Karthik and Ben for procurement and vendor cadence detail. Sending a short Mx to agree on an action plan and then we'll produce a staggered fulfillment proposal. Attaching a draft Redwood dedicated proposal for structure.

Attachments: Redwood-dedicated-proposal-v1.pdf

—Rachel
Rachel Kim
Head of Customer Solutions, Redwood Inference
From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2025-10-30T11:28:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Dedicated pool sizing + ability to frontload procurement

Internal —

Forwarding Tim's RFP. Quick notes / proposed approach (we'll summarize to NovaApps on the call):

- Ask: They want to shrink time-to-capacity risk by frontloading OEM orders for a fraction of required GPUs and bridging with cloud brokerage for steady-state peaks.
- OEM lead time baseline: historically 12–18 weeks for the SKU they requested. If we can source an alternate SKU (same memory band, different board) we can sometimes compress to 8–10 weeks but need perf validation.
- Proposal: split into tranches: T1 = 30% of committed capacity (OEM expedited if possible), T2 = 50% 8–12 wks, T3 = remaining via normal queue + cloud backstop for spikes.
- Commercial: offer a staged reserved contract with a ramp schedule + explicit cloud credit / burst-price clause to avoid SLA gaps.

Action items:
- Karthik: can you pull current OEM queue signal and confirm whether we can get a partial expedite on the 30% tranche? Also sanity-check customs/import delta.
- Ben: please prepare a variant quote (see suggested SKU swap) and include a rapid-ship premium option in the spreadsheet (will attach).
- Laura: coordinate internal ops constraints (staging pool, image baking timeline) if we need to accept mixed SKUs.

I'll propose a 30-minute call with Tim later today.
